description: BPSC TRE Computer Science Model Test Paper 05 containing 150 questions across Language, General Studies, and Computer Science.

questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: "He had to repent _______ his hasty decision."
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The verb 'repent' is commonly followed by the preposition 'of' when expressing regret for a mistake or wrongdoing.

questions.questionText: Identify the part of speech of the underlined word: "He walked fast to catch the morning train."
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: In this sentence, 'fast' modifies the verb 'walked', functioning as an adverb of manner.

questions.questionText: Choose the word closest in meaning (synonym) to "EPHEMERAL":
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Transient, short-lived, and fleeting are all valid synonyms of 'ephemeral'.

questions.questionText: A person who is indifferent to pain or pleasure is termed as a:
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: A stoic is someone who endures pain or hardship without showing feelings or complaining.

questions.questionText: Select the correct passive voice: "Someone stole my pen yesterday."
questions.optionB: My pen had been stolen yesterday.
questions.optionC: My pen is stolen by someone yesterday.
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The past simple 'stole' converts to 'was stolen' in passive voice.

questions.questionText: Which of the following sentences contains an error?
questions.optionA: Neither of the two boys have submitted his assignment.
questions.optionB: Each of the girls sings well.
questions.optionC: Ten miles is a long distance to walk.
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: 'Neither' takes a singular verb, so 'have submitted' should be 'has submitted'.

questions.questionText: Mother of one's spouse is called:
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The mother of one's husband or wife is one's mother-in-law.

questions.questionText: If the 1st of a month falls on Friday, what day will be the 25th of that same month?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Days passed = 25 - 1 = 24. 24 mod 7 = 3 odd days. Friday + 3 days = Monday.

questions.questionText: 'श, ष, स, ह' व्यंजनों को किस वर्ग में रखा जाता है?
questions.optionD: उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanation: जिन व्यंजनों के उच्चारण में हवा मुख से रगड़ खाकर ऊष्मा पैदा करती है, उन्हें ऊष्म या संघर्षी व्यंजन कहते हैं।

questions.questionText: 'वागीश' शब्द का शुद्ध संधि-विच्छेद क्या होगा?
questions.optionD: उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanation: व्यंजन संधि के नियमानुसार 'क्' के बाद स्वर आने पर 'क्' का 'ग्' हो जाता है (वाक् + ईश = वागीश)।

questions.questionText: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा शब्द 'द्वंद्व समास' का सही उदाहरण है?
questions.optionD: उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanation: दाल-रोटी, माता-पिता और रुपया-पैसा तीनों में दोनों पद प्रधान हैं, अतः ये द्वंद्व समास के उदाहरण हैं।

questions.questionText: 'मृगेंद्र' किसका पर्यायवाची शब्द है?
questions.optionD: उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanation: मृगों (पशुओं) का राजा अर्थात् सिंह या शेर को 'मृगेंद्र' कहा जाता है।

questions.questionText: 'तिमिर' शब्द का सही विलोम शब्द क्या होगा?
questions.optionD: उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanation: 'तिमिर' का अर्थ अंधकार होता है, जिसके विलोम प्रकाश, आलोक और ज्योति तीनों हो सकते हैं।

questions.questionText: 'जिसकी आशा न की गई हो' वाक्यांश के लिए एक शब्द है:
questions.optionD: उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanation: जिसकी पूर्व से कोई आशा न की गई हो, उसे 'अप्रत्याशित' कहते हैं।

questions.questionText: 'आस्तीन का सांप' मुहावरे का सही भावार्थ है:
questions.optionA: निकट रहकर कपट करने वाला मित्र
questions.optionD: उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanation: 'आस्तीन का सांप' का अर्थ साथ रहकर विश्वासघात या कपट करने वाला व्यक्ति होता है।

questions.questionText: निम्नलिखित में से शुद्ध वर्तनी वाले शब्द का चयन कीजिए:
questions.optionD: उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanation: विद्वान का स्त्रीलिंग रूप शुद्ध वर्तनी में 'विदुषी' लिखा जाता है।

questions.questionText: 'राम ने रावण को बाण से मारा।' इस वाक्य में 'बाण से' में कौन-सा कारक है?
questions.optionD: उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanation: क्रिया के साधन या उपकरण के रूप में 'बाण से' प्रयुक्त हुआ है, अतः यहाँ करण कारक है।

questions.questionText: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा शब्द विदेशी (आगत) शब्द है?
questions.optionD: उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanation: वकील (अरबी), कैंची (तुर्की) और अलमारी (पुर्तगाली) तीनों ही विदेशी भाषा से आए आगत शब्द हैं।

questions.questionText: 'अत्युत्तम' शब्द में कौन-सी संधि है?
questions.optionD: उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanation: अति + उत्तम = अत्युत्तम (इ + उ = यु), जो यण् स्वर संधि का नियम है।

questions.questionText: "कनक कनक ते सौ गुनी मादकता अधिकाय। या खाए बौराय जग या पाए बौराय।।" इस दोहे में कौन-सा अलंकार है?
questions.optionD: उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanation: 'कनक' शब्द दो बार आया है और दोनों बार उसके अर्थ भिन्न हैं (धतूरा और सोना), अतः यमक अलंकार है।

questions.questionText: 'चौराहा' शब्द में कौन-सा समास है?
questions.optionD: उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanation: 'चार राहों का समाहार'—यहाँ पूर्वपद संख्यावाचक होने से द्विगु समास है।

questions.questionText: निम्नलिखित में से नित्य एकवचन में प्रयुक्त होने वाला शब्द कौन-सा है?
questions.optionD: उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanation: जनता, वर्षा और पानी तीनों द्रव्यवाचक/समूहवाचक शब्द नित्य एकवचन में प्रयुक्त होते हैं।

questions.questionText: 'नौ दो ग्यारह होना' मुहावरे का सही अर्थ है:
questions.optionD: उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanation: 'नौ दो ग्यारह होना' का अर्थ रफूचक्कर होना या भाग जाना होता है।

questions.questionText: 'अनुराग' का विलोम शब्द है:
questions.optionD: उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanation: 'अनुराग' (प्रेम) का विलोम शब्द 'विराग' होता है।

questions.questionText: 'अनल' और 'अनिल' शब्द युग्म का सही अर्थ-भेद क्या है?
questions.optionD: उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanation: 'अनल' का अर्थ आग (अग्नि) और 'अनिल' का अर्थ हवा (वायु) होता है।

questions.questionText: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा शब्द 'सरस्वती' का पर्यायवाची नहीं है?
questions.optionD: उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanation: भारती और शारदा सरस्वती जी के पर्यायवाची हैं, जबकि 'पद्मा' लक्ष्मी जी का पर्यायवाची है।

questions.questionText: 'पराजय' शब्द में कौन-सा उपसर्ग प्रयुक्त हुआ है?
questions.optionD: उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanation: परा + जय = पराजय। इसमें 'परा' उपसर्ग जुड़ा है।

questions.questionText: 'जो इंद्रियों द्वारा न जाना जा सके' वाक्यांश के लिए एक शब्द है:
questions.optionD: उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanation: इंद्रियों की पहुँच से परे होने वाले के लिए 'अगोचर' और 'अतींद्रिय' दोनों शब्दों का प्रयोग होता है।

questions.questionText: 'वह अभी-अभी आया है।' वाक्य में किस काल का बोध होता है?
questions.optionD: उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanation: क्रिया के जिस रूप से यह पता चले कि कार्य अभी-अभी कुछ समय पहले समाप्त हुआ है, उसे आसन्न भूतकाल कहते हैं।

questions.questionText: 'तू डाल-डाल, मैं पात-पात' लोकोक्ति का सही अभिप्राय है:
questions.optionA: दोनों चालाक होना / एक से बढ़कर दूसरा चालाक
questions.optionD: उपर्युक्त में से एक से अधिक
questions.explanation: इस लोकोक्ति का अर्थ एक की तुलना में दूसरे का अधिक होशियार या चालाक होना है।

questions.questionText: A cistern can be filled by two pipes $X$ and $Y$ in 20 minutes and 30 minutes respectively, while a third pipe $Z$ can empty the full tank in 15 minutes. If all three are opened together, in how many minutes will the tank be full?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Net rate = 1/20 + 1/30 - 1/15 = (3 + 2 - 4)/60 = 1/60. Hence, it takes 60 minutes.

questions.questionText: Find the remainder when $2^{100}$ is divided by 7:
questions.optionD: More than one of the above

questions.questionText: The ratio of water and milk in a 60-litre mixture is 1:3. How much water (in litres) must be added so that the ratio of water to milk becomes 1:2?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above

questions.questionText: The difference between the Compound Interest and Simple Interest on a sum of money for 2 years at 8% per annum is Rs. 64. What is the principal sum?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above

questions.questionText: A metallic sphere of radius 6 cm is melted and recast into small spherical balls each of radius 1 cm. How many such balls can be formed?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Number of balls = Volume_large / Volume_small = (4/3 π 6^3) / (4/3 π 1^3) = 6^3 / 1^3 = 216.

questions.questionText: A boat covers 24 km upstream and 36 km downstream in 6 hours. If the speed of the stream is 2 km/h, what is the speed of the boat in still water?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Let boat speed = b. 24/(b - 2) + 36/(b + 2) = 6. Testing b = 10: 24/8 + 36/12 = 3 + 3 = 6 hours.

questions.questionText: If $\log_{10} 2 = 0.3010$, what is the number of digits in $2^{50}$?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above

questions.questionText: The angles of a quadrilateral are in the ratio $2:3:5:8$. What is the measure of the smallest angle?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Total ratio units = 2 + 3 + 5 + 8 = 18. 18x = 360° => x = 20°. Smallest angle = 2 * 20° = 40°.

questions.questionText: Heavy water ($\text{D}_2\text{O}$) is employed in nuclear power reactors as a:
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Heavy water acts as both a neutron moderator and a thermal coolant in pressurized heavy-water reactors.

questions.questionText: Why does sky appear blue to an observer on Earth during daytime?
questions.optionA: Rayleigh scattering of sunlight by fine atmospheric molecules, where shorter wavelengths scatter most
questions.optionB: Total internal reflection in upper ionosphere
questions.optionC: Absorption of red spectrum by water droplets
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Atmospheric gas molecules scatter shorter blue wavelengths much more than longer red wavelengths per Rayleigh scattering.

questions.questionText: Which vitamin deficiency in human diet causes Pernicious Anaemia?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Pernicious anaemia is caused by an inability to absorb or an inadequate dietary intake of Vitamin B12.

questions.questionText: What is the fundamental working principle behind an Optical Fiber cable?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Optical fibers confine light within the high-index core via successive total internal reflections at the core-cladding boundary.

questions.questionText: Plaster of Paris (POP) has the chemical formula:
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Plaster of Paris is calcium sulphate hemihydrate, with chemical formula CaSO4·1/2H2O.

questions.questionText: Which part of the human brain controls involuntary vital functions such as heartbeat, blood pressure, and peristalsis?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The medulla oblongata in the brainstem houses cardiac, vasomotor, and respiratory reflex centers.

questions.questionText: What is the escape velocity from the surface of the Earth approximately equal to?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The minimum speed required to escape Earth's gravitational field is approximately 11.2 km/s.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an example of an amphoteric oxide?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Both Al2O3 and ZnO can react with both acidic and basic solutions, exhibiting amphoteric behavior.

questions.questionText: Who has been conferred the 58th Jnanpith Award?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The 58th Jnanpith Award was jointly conferred upon poet Gulzar (Urdu) and Sanskrit scholar Jagadguru Rambhadracharya.

questions.questionText: In which Indian state is the world's largest renewable energy park (Khavda Renewable Energy Park) being developed?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The 30 GW hybrid renewable energy park is being constructed at Khavda in the Kutch district of Gujarat.

questions.questionText: What is the name of the deep-sea human submersible vehicle under India's 'Samudrayaan Mission'?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Matsya 6000 is an indigenously developed human submersible designed to carry three personnel to a depth of 6,000 meters.

questions.questionText: Which country has officially become the 32nd member nation of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO)?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Sweden officially deposited its instrument of accession to become NATO's 32nd member in March 2024.

questions.questionText: Project 'Namo Bharat' in India is associated with:
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: 'Namo Bharat' is the branding assigned to the train sets operating on the Delhi–Meerut Regional Rapid Transit System.

questions.questionText: The Ramsar site 'Sirpur Wetland' is located in which state of India?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Sirpur Lake/Wetland is an artificial wetland located in Indore, Madhya Pradesh.

questions.questionText: The 'Ten Degree Channel' separates which of the following geographical regions?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The Ten Degree Channel is a 150 km wide strait separating the Andaman Islands from the Nicobar Islands.

questions.questionText: Which river in India is termed as 'Vridha Ganga' or 'Dakshin Ganga'?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The Godavari is known as Vridha Ganga or Dakshin Ganga owing to its age, length, and cultural significance.

questions.questionText: The Majuli island, the world's largest inhabited freshwater riverine island, is situated on which river?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Majuli is formed by the Brahmaputra River and its anabranches in upper Assam.

questions.questionText: In Bihar, which district has the lowest sex ratio as per the 2011 Census?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Munger recorded the lowest sex ratio in Bihar according to the 2011 Census with 876 females per 1000 males.

questions.questionText: The Kusheshwar Asthan Bird Sanctuary is situated in which district of Bihar?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Kusheshwar Asthan Bird Sanctuary covers seasonal wetland areas in Darbhanga district.

questions.questionText: Which plateau region of Bihar contains rich geological reserves of Dharwar rock formations?
questions.optionB: Southern hills of Gaya, Nawada, and Munger
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Dharwar cratonic rocks in Bihar outcrop along the southern hill belt of Gaya, Nawada, Jamui, and Munger.

questions.questionText: In which district of Bihar was the historic 'Dighwara copper plate inscription' discovered?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The Dighwara copper plate of the Pratihara king Mahendrapala I was unearthed in Saran district.

questions.questionText: The Someshwar Range in West Champaran forms the international border between Bihar and:
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The Someshwar hills form the international boundary dividing northwestern Bihar from Nepal.

questions.questionText: Who was the British Governor-General who enacted the 'Abolition of Sati Act' in 1829?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Lord William Bentinck promulgated Bengal Sati Regulation XVII in 1829, declaring the practice illegal.

questions.questionText: Who authored the famous economic critique 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India' expounding the Drain of Wealth theory?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Dadabhai Naoroji wrote this foundational economic work detailing the transfer of Indian surplus to Britain.

questions.questionText: Which revolutionary organization was established by Surya Sen that carried out the historic Chittagong Armoury Raid in 1930?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Masterda Surya Sen led the raid under the banner of the Indian Republican Army, Chittagong Branch.

questions.questionText: Who founded the 'All India Untouchability League' (later renamed Harijan Sevak Sangh) in 1932?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Mahatma Gandhi established the organization in 1932 following the Poona Pact to eradicate untouchability.

questions.questionText: Which commission was sent to British India in 1928 that faced massive black-flag protests because it had no Indian members?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The Indian Statutory Commission headed by Sir John Simon was boycotted nationwide because it had an all-white composition.

questions.questionText: Who started the famous nationalist journal 'Al-Hilal' in 1912?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Maulana Abul Kalam Azad founded the Urdu weekly newspaper 'Al-Hilal' in Calcutta to promote anti-colonial unity.

questions.questionText: In Bihar, who organized the famous 'Salt Satyagraha' in Champaran and Saran simultaneously in April 1930?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Bipin Bihari Varma led the Salt Satyagraha in Champaran and Saran districts in April 1930.

questions.questionText: Who was elected President of the historic Ramgarh Session of the Indian National Congress held in 1940 (then part of Bihar)?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Maulana Abul Kalam Azad was elected Congress President at the 53rd session in Ramgarh (now in Jharkhand).

questions.questionText: The famous 'Chauri Chaura' incident that caused Gandhiji to suspend the Non-Cooperation Movement occurred in which year?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The violent clash at Chauri Chaura took place on 4 February 1922, prompting Gandhi to call off the movement.

questions.questionText: Who among the following founded the 'Patna Yuvak Sangh' in 1927 to inspire nationalist youth?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Manindra Narayan Roy founded the Patna Yuvak Sangh in 1927 as a youth wing for nationalist and revolutionary activities.

questions.questionText: How many minterms are present in the minimal canonical SOP expansion of a 3-variable Boolean function $F(A, B, C) = \Sigma m(0, 2, 4, 6)$?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The canonical sum-of-minterms form explicitly lists the 4 designated minterms: m0, m2, m4, and m6.

questions.questionText: A combinational circuit has 4 inputs ($A, B, C, D$). What is the essential prime implicant of the minterm list $m(0, 1, 2, 3, 8, 9, 10, 11)$?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Combining the two 4-cells from the top and bottom rows where B = 0 yields the single literal term B'.

questions.questionText: What is the characteristic equation of an edge-triggered SR flip-flop?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The characteristic equation of an SR flip-flop is Q(next) = S + R'Q, subject to the invalidity constraint SR = 0.

questions.questionText: An 8-bit ripple carry adder consists of 8 full adders cascaded in series. If each full adder has a sum generation delay of 12 ns and a carry generation delay of 8 ns, what is the worst-case propagation delay for computing the final carry-out?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Carry out ripples through 8 stages sequentially: 8 * 8 ns = 64 ns.

questions.questionText: What is the minimum number of select lines required for a demultiplexer that has 1 input and 64 outputs?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: For 2^n outputs, n select lines are needed. 2^6 = 64, so 6 select lines are required.

questions.questionText: In Booth's signed binary multiplication algorithm, when the current bit pair $(Q_n, Q_{n+1})$ is 0 1, what arithmetic operation is performed on the accumulator ($A$)?
questions.optionC: Arithmetic shift right only without addition
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: In Booth's algorithm, transition 01 represents the end of a block of ones, triggering A = A + M before shifting.

questions.questionText: In IEEE 754 Double Precision floating point format, how many bits are reserved for the exponent and mantissa (significand) respectively?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: IEEE 754 64-bit double precision reserves 1 sign bit, 11 exponent bits, and 52 fraction/mantissa bits.

questions.questionText: A processor features a 5-stage instruction pipeline (IF, ID, EX, MEM, WB). Each stage takes 1 clock cycle of 2 ns. How much total time is required to execute 100 independent instructions in an ideal pipeline without branch or data stalls?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Total clock cycles = k + n - 1 = 5 + 100 - 1 = 104 cycles. Total execution time = 104 * 2 ns = 208 ns.

questions.questionText: A computer system employs a 2-level memory hierarchy consisting of cache memory and main memory. The cache access time is 2 ns, main memory access time is 50 ns, and cache hit ratio is 0.95. What is the average memory access time (AMAT) assuming simultaneous access?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: AMAT = t_cache + (1 - h) * t_memory = 2 + 0.05 * 50 = 2 + 2.5 = 4.5 ns.

questions.questionText: In an auto-increment addressing mode, when is the register operand incremented?
questions.optionB: After its value is used to access memory (Post-increment)
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: In standard auto-increment addressing, the memory access occurs using the current register pointer, which is then incremented.

questions.questionText: Which memory organization uses a CAM (Content Addressable Memory) cell array to compare search data against all entries in a single clock cycle?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Fully associative caches utilize parallel CAM hardware to search tag matches across every entry concurrently.

questions.questionText: What is the primary characteristic of a Princeton (von Neumann) architecture compared to Harvard architecture?
questions.optionA: Unified physical bus and memory for both instruction and data
questions.optionB: Separate independent memory spaces and buses for instructions and data
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Von Neumann architecture uses a shared common memory space and bus system for both instructions and operational data.

questions.questionText: In DMA controllers, what is "Cycle Stealing" mode?
questions.optionA: DMA controller takes complete charge of the bus until an entire multi-block file is copied
questions.optionB: DMA controller acquires bus control from the CPU for the transfer of exactly one memory word per request, then yields it back
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: In cycle stealing, the DMA controller interleaves single-word transfers into CPU bus cycles without seizing the bus entirely.

questions.questionText: In microprogrammed CPU design, horizontal microcode differs from vertical microcode because:
questions.optionA: Horizontal microinstructions provide unencoded control bits for each control signal, maximizing parallelism at the cost of wider control words
questions.optionB: Horizontal microcode is encoded and requires decoders
questions.optionC: Horizontal microcode executes more slowly than vertical
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Horizontal microcode allocates dedicated control bits without encoding, enabling wide parallel control without decoder latency.

questions.questionText: What is the parity bit configuration used in Hamming Error-Correction Code for single-bit correction of a 7-bit data block ($D_1$ to $D_7$)?
questions.optionA: Parity bits are placed at bit positions that are powers of 2 (1, 2, 4, 8)
questions.optionB: Parity bits are placed strictly at the beginning and end only
questions.optionC: Parity bits are derived by simple modulo 10 checksum
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: In standard Hamming (11, 7) code, check parity bits reside at bit indices that are powers of 2: 1, 2, 4, and 8.

questions.explanation: &arr + 1 advances the pointer past all 5 elements. Stepping back by 2 ints (p - 2) points to arr[3] = 40.

questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: 2[a] is equivalent to *(2 + a) = *(a + 2) = a[2], which evaluates to 15.

questions.questionText: Consider the function pointer declaration: void (*signal(int, void (*)(int)))(int);. What does this describe?
questions.optionA: A function that takes an integer and a function pointer, and returns a function pointer taking an integer and returning void
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The signal() function accepts an int and a sighandler_t pointer, and returns the previous sighandler_t pointer.

questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Dereferencing pointer 'p' after calling free(p) violates memory safety, producing undefined behavior.

questions.questionText: In modern C++, what is the significant performance advantage of "Move Semantics" introduced with rvalue references (Type&&)?
questions.optionA: Eliminating unnecessary deep copies of dynamic resources by transferring ownership directly
questions.optionC: Forcing member functions to execute on GPU
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Move semantics avoid expensive heap copies of temporary objects by stealing ownership of internal pointers.

questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Instantiating three objects (t1, t2, t3) increments the static member variable 'count' three times, yielding 3.

questions.questionText: What problem does the "Diamond Problem" in C++ multiple inheritance cause if virtual base classes are NOT used?
questions.optionA: Compilation fails due to ambiguous member access and duplicate copies of the grandparent class subobject
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Without virtual inheritance, two copies of the base class subobject are created, causing compiler ambiguity on member accesses.

questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The virtual method dispatch table routes the call on the actual heap-allocated object of type C to C::print().

questions.questionText: What is a "Smart Pointer" in C++ STL that represents exclusive, non-shareable ownership of a dynamically allocated resource?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: std::unique_ptr enforces sole ownership of an object; it cannot be copied, only moved.

questions.questionText: In C++, if a class allocates raw heap memory in its constructor, what rule dictates that it must also explicitly declare a Destructor, Copy Constructor, and Copy Assignment Operator?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The Rule of Three states that managing custom resources requires defining a destructor, copy constructor, and copy assignment operator.

questions.explanation: Loop prints 0 and 1, skips 2 via continue, prints 3, and breaks when reaching 4, producing '0 1 3 '.

questions.questionText: In C++, which operator cannot be overloaded under any circumstance?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: C++ forbids overloading the operators: sizeof, typeid, .*, ::, and ?:.

questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Since 'val' was originally defined as non-const, removing const via const_cast and writing to it is defined and prints 50.

questions.questionText: What happens when an exception is thrown in a C++ constructor before the constructor finishes initialization?
questions.optionA: The corresponding destructor for that partially constructed object is NOT called, potentially causing memory leaks unless smart pointers are used
questions.optionB: Destructor is called automatically on the uninitialized memory
questions.optionC: Entire program aborts with a segmentation fault
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: If a constructor throws, the object is considered unconstructed, so its destructor does not execute.

questions.questionText: In C++, what is a lambda expression capture clause [&] specified for?
questions.optionA: Capturing all enclosing automatic variables by reference
questions.optionB: Capturing all enclosing automatic variables by value
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: [&] instructs the compiler to capture all accessible local automatic variables by reference.

questions.questionText: Which function in C standard library compares two memory blocks byte-by-byte regardless of null termination?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: memcmp compares up to n specified bytes of two memory areas without stopping at null terminators.

questions.questionText: In C++, template specialization allows:
questions.optionA: Defining an entirely customized class or function implementation for a specific data type
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Template specialization overrides the generic template with custom behavior for specific types.

questions.questionText: What is the fundamental difference between dynamic binding and static binding?
questions.optionA: Static binding is resolved at compile-time using variable types; dynamic binding is resolved at runtime based on actual object types via vtables
questions.optionB: Dynamic binding makes code run 10x faster
questions.optionC: Static binding occurs only in interpreted languages
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Static binding connects calls at compilation, whereas dynamic binding uses vtables at runtime to invoke overrides.

questions.questionText: What will happen if the derived class destructor is not declared virtual when destroying a derived object via a base class pointer?
questions.optionA: Only the base class destructor will execute, leading to resource leaks in the derived class
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Deleting via a Base* lacking a virtual destructor causes static binding to ~Base(), skipping the derived destructor.

questions.questionText: In C++, which container adapter guarantees Last-In-First-Out (LIFO) access to elements?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: std::stack provides LIFO access with push, pop, and top operations.

questions.questionText: In an undirected graph $G = (V, E)$, what does the Handshaking Lemma state?
questions.optionC: Total odd degree vertices in any graph must be an odd number
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Every edge contributes two endpoints, so the sum of vertex degrees equals twice the total number of edges.

questions.questionText: An array of $N$ elements is sorted in ascending order. If we run the Randomized QuickSort algorithm, what is its expected (average) time complexity?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Randomized pivot selection avoids the worst-case degradation on presorted inputs, maintaining an expected O(N log N) runtime.

questions.questionText: What is the time complexity of the Floyd-Warshall algorithm for finding all-pairs shortest paths in a directed graph having $V$ vertices?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Floyd-Warshall runs three nested loops over all vertices, giving a strict time complexity of Θ(V^3).

questions.questionText: What is the worst-case number of rotations required during an insertion operation into an AVL tree?
questions.optionA: At most 2 rotations (either single or double rotation)
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Inserting a key requires at most one single or one double rotation (2 basic rotations) to restore AVL balance.

questions.questionText: In a B-Tree of order $M$ (where $M$ is the maximum number of children a node can have), what is the minimum number of keys any non-root internal node must hold?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Non-root internal nodes in a B-Tree of order M must have at least ceil(M/2) children and ceil(M/2) - 1 keys.

questions.questionText: What is the time complexity of finding the strongly connected components (SCC) of a directed graph using Kosaraju’s algorithm?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Kosaraju's algorithm executes two passes of DFS along with graph transposition, running in linear O(V + E) time.

questions.questionText: Which data structure is used to implement a Trie (Prefix Tree) efficiently for dictionary search?
questions.optionA: Multiway tree where edges or child pointers correspond to alphabet characters
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: A Trie is a tree where each node branches based on alphabet characters to store string prefixes.

questions.questionText: Using Master Theorem, solve the recurrence: $T(N) = 3T(N/4) + N \log N$:
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: log_4(3) ≈ 0.793. f(N) = N log N dominates N^0.793 polynomially, satisfying Master Theorem Case 3 to give Θ(N log N).

questions.questionText: What is the worst-case time complexity of standard Radix Sort when sorting $N$ numbers with $d$ digits each, using counting sort as subroutine?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Radix sort runs Counting Sort across d digit passes, with total complexity O(d * (N + k)).

questions.questionText: A Hamiltonian Path in an undirected graph is a path that:
questions.optionB: Visits every vertex in the graph exactly once
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: A Hamiltonian path visits each vertex in the graph exactly once without repeating vertices.

questions.questionText: In an open-addressing hash table with load factor $\alpha = n/m$ where $\alpha < 1$, what is the average number of probes required in an unsuccessful search assuming uniform hashing?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Under uniform hashing, an unsuccessful search checks an expected 1 / (1 - α) slots before finding an empty slot.

questions.questionText: What problem arises when using DFS to search for a goal node in an infinite or extremely deep state-space tree?
questions.optionA: It may get trapped in an infinite branch and never terminate, making it incomplete
questions.optionC: It always finds the optimal path
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: DFS can traverse indefinitely down an infinite left path without backtracking, rendering it incomplete.

questions.questionText: Which algorithm solves the fractional knapsack problem optimally?
questions.optionB: Greedy Algorithm (sorting items by value-to-weight ratio)
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Fractional knapsack exhibits the greedy-choice property and is solved optimally by picking items with highest value/weight.

questions.questionText: What is an articulation point (cut vertex) in a connected graph?
questions.optionA: A vertex whose removal increases the number of connected components of the graph
questions.optionC: A leaf node in a spanning tree
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: An articulation point is a vertex whose deletion disconnects the graph or increases its number of connected components.

questions.questionText: Which data structure supports Find and Union operations with almost linear time complexity $\alpha(N)$ (inverse Ackermann function)?
questions.optionA: Disjoint Set Union (DSU) with Path Compression and Union by Rank
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: DSU equipped with path compression and rank heuristics bounds m operations on n elements to O(m * α(n)).

questions.questionText: Consider a relation $R(A, B, C, D)$ with functional dependencies: $F = \{A \rightarrow B, B \rightarrow C, C \rightarrow D, D \rightarrow A\}$. What is the candidate key for $R$?
questions.optionC: Every single attribute $A, B, C, D$ is individually a candidate key
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Because of the cyclic dependency chain, the closure of each individual attribute encompasses {A, B, C, D}.

questions.questionText: In relational calculus, a query that produces an infinite number of tuples is called:
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: An unsafe relational calculus expression yields results outside the active domain, generating an infinite relation.

questions.questionText: If a relation is in 3NF and every determinant is a candidate key, then the relation is guaranteed to be in:
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The definition of BCNF requires that for every functional dependency X -> Y, X must be a superkey.

questions.questionText: What is the fundamental difference between Conflict Serializability and View Serializability?
questions.optionA: Every view serializable schedule is conflict serializable
questions.optionB: Every conflict serializable schedule is view serializable, but not all view serializable schedules are conflict serializable (due to blind writes)
questions.optionC: View serializability can be tested in polynomial time, while conflict serializability is NP-complete
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Conflict serializability is a strict subset of view serializability; schedules with blind writes may be view serializable without being conflict serializable.

questions.questionText: In database transactions, what is the Strict Two-Phase Locking (Strict 2PL) protocol?
questions.optionA: A transaction releases locks as soon as operations complete
questions.optionB: A transaction must hold all its exclusive locks (X-locks) until the transaction commits or aborts
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Strict 2PL requires all exclusive locks to be held until the end of transaction (commit/abort), preventing cascading aborts.

questions.questionText: What does the SQL clause DENSE_RANK() do compared to RANK()?
questions.optionA: DENSE_RANK() does not leave gaps in ranking values in case of ties
questions.optionC: DENSE_RANK() resets ranks after every 10 rows
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: DENSE_RANK() assigns consecutive integer rankings without gaps when handling tied values.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is true regarding a Clustered Index in an RDBMS?
questions.optionA: The physical storage order of rows in the table matches the index order
questions.optionB: A table can have at most one clustered index
questions.optionC: Leaf nodes of a clustered index contain the actual data rows
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: A table has only one clustered index, its leaf nodes store the table rows, and records are sorted physically by the indexed key.

questions.questionText: What is the function of the checkpoint mechanism in database recovery systems?
questions.optionA: It flushes all dirty log records and modified buffer blocks to disk, allowing the recovery engine to ignore log records before the checkpoint during restart
questions.optionB: It aborts uncommitted transactions after 10 seconds
questions.optionC: It creates duplicate copies of primary keys
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Checkpoints periodically sync memory buffers to disk to reduce log scanning and redo time during crash recovery.

questions.questionText: What relational algebra expression corresponds to the SQL EXCEPT (or MINUS) operator between relations $R$ and $S$?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The relational set difference operator R - S represents tuples in relation R that do not appear in S.

questions.questionText: What is an index seek versus an index scan in database query execution?
questions.optionA: Index seek traverses the B-Tree directly using search criteria, reading only matching rows; index scan reads the entire index tree sequentially
questions.optionB: Index scan is always faster than index seek
questions.optionC: Index seek requires scanning all table pages
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: An index seek navigates the index tree to pinpoint specific qualifying rows, whereas an index scan traverses the entire index.

questions.questionText: In SQL, what happens when a query performs an arithmetic operation involving a NULL value (e.g., SALARY + NULL)?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Under three-valued logic, any arithmetic expression involving an unknown/NULL operand evaluates to NULL.

questions.questionText: What is lossless-join decomposition property?
questions.optionA: When a relation $R$ is decomposed into $R_1$ and $R_2$, joining them back produces exactly the original relation without spurious tuples ($R_1 \bowtie R_2 = R$)
questions.optionB: Memory is never leaked during a join query
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: A decomposition is lossless if natural join of the projection relations reconstructs the original instance without extra or missing tuples.

questions.questionText: A system has 4 processes and 6 instances of a single resource type. Each process needs at most 2 instances of the resource. Can a deadlock occur in this system?
questions.optionB: No, the system is completely deadlock-free
questions.optionC: Deadlock occurs only if preemption is enabled
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Peak demand is 4 * (2 - 1) + 1 = 5. Since 6 instances are available (> 5), deadlock is impossible.

questions.questionText: What is the fundamental difference between Hard Real-Time Systems and Soft Real-Time Systems?
questions.optionA: In hard real-time systems, missing a single deadline results in total system catastrophe, whereas in soft real-time systems, missing a deadline degrades quality of service
questions.optionB: Hard real-time systems run only on 64-bit Linux
questions.optionC: Soft real-time systems never use priority scheduling
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Hard real-time deadlines must be met with zero tolerance for failure, whereas soft real-time accommodates occasional missed deadlines.

questions.questionText: Consider a 32-bit virtual address architecture with a two-level page table. If the page size is 4 KB ($2^{12}$ bytes) and each page table entry takes 4 bytes, how are the address bits divided for (Page Dir, Page Table, Offset)?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Offset = 12 bits. A 4 KB page holds 4 KB / 4 B = 1024 entries = 10 bits. The remaining 32 - 12 - 10 = 10 bits form the top directory.

questions.questionText: What is the major drawback of the Shortest Job First (SJF) scheduling algorithm?
questions.optionA: It causes long turnaround times for short jobs
questions.optionB: It is difficult to predict the length of the next CPU burst in advance, and long processes may suffer from starvation
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Future CPU burst lengths cannot be known in advance, and long jobs risk indefinite postponement (starvation).

questions.questionText: Peterson's Solution is a classical software-based algorithm designed to solve the Critical Section problem for how many concurrent processes?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Peterson's algorithm is formulated specifically for mutual exclusion between two cooperating processes.

questions.questionText: In the Linux kernel, what mechanism is executed to complete the deferrable, non-time-critical part of an interrupt handler?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Bottom-half routines (tasklets, workqueues, softirqs) process deferred non-critical interrupt work with interrupts re-enabled.

questions.questionText: What is an Inode in Unix/Linux file systems?
questions.optionA: A data structure that stores all metadata about a file (permissions, size, owner, data block pointers) except its filename and actual content
questions.optionC: A physical sector on an SSD
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: An index node (inode) maintains file ownership, mode, timestamps, and block addresses, leaving the filename in the directory entry.

questions.questionText: Which page replacement algorithm suffers from Belady's Anomaly where allocating more page frames increases page faults?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: FIFO is a non-stack algorithm and can exhibit Belady's anomaly, unlike stack algorithms such as LRU.

questions.questionText: What is the purpose of the mmap() system call in Unix-like operating systems?
questions.optionA: Maps files or devices directly into the calling process's virtual memory address space
questions.optionC: Compiles C++ code into kernel binaries
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: mmap() binds file data directly to pages in process virtual memory, facilitating direct memory reads/writes without read() buffers.

questions.questionText: Priority Inversion problem in real-time operating systems is solved using which protocol?
questions.optionA: Priority Ceiling Protocol / Priority Inheritance Protocol
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Priority Inheritance dynamically elevates a low-priority thread holding a contested mutex to the priority of the waiting high-priority thread.

questions.questionText: In a Stop-and-Wait ARQ protocol, if the round-trip propagation time ($2 \times T_p$) is 40 ms and frame transmission time ($T_t$) is 10 ms, what is the maximum channel utilization (efficiency $\eta$)?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above

questions.questionText: In IPv4 subnetting, how many usable host IP addresses are available in a subnet with CIDR prefix /28?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Host bits = 32 - 28 = 4. Total IPs = 2^4 = 16. Subtracting network and broadcast addresses leaves 16 - 2 = 14 usable hosts.

questions.questionText: What algorithm is utilized by the TCP protocol to avoid network congestion and discover available link bandwidth dynamically?
questions.optionA: Slow Start, Congestion Avoidance, Fast Retransmit, and Fast Recovery
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: TCP implements congestion control using the state machine of Slow Start, Congestion Avoidance, Fast Retransmit, and Fast Recovery.

questions.questionText: In asymmetric public-key cryptography using RSA algorithm, if chosen prime numbers are $p = 3$ and $q = 11$, what is Euler's totient function $\phi(n)$?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above

questions.questionText: Which of the following grammars generates the language $L = \{a^n b^n \mid n \ge 1\}$?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: The language requires counting and matching balanced symbols, which is generated by the CFG production S -> aSb | ab.

questions.questionText: Which software engineering metric measures the degree of functional interrelatedness of elements within a single software module?
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Cohesion measures how focused and closely related the responsibilities of a single software module are.

questions.questionText: In Web Security, Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attacks occur primarily when:
questions.optionA: An attacker injects malicious client-side scripts (such as JavaScript) into trusted web pages viewed by other users
questions.optionB: An attacker executes raw SQL queries directly on back-end tables
questions.optionC: A web server runs out of TCP port allocations
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: XSS occurs when malicious scripts are injected into web pages and executed within victims' client-side browser contexts.

questions.questionText: A Turing Machine differs fundamentally from a Pushdown Automaton (PDA) because:
questions.optionA: A Turing Machine has an infinite read/write tape that can move in both left and right directions, giving it unbounded computational capability
questions.optionB: A Turing Machine cannot handle nondeterminism
questions.optionC: A PDA recognizes all recursively enumerable languages
questions.optionD: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Unlike the restrictive LIFO stack access of a PDA, a Turing machine features a bidirectional tape for arbitrary read/write access.
